title: Driverless cars
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.answer: D — Potentially, fully automated taxis are more cost-effective than normal taxis.
questions.answerKey: D — Potentially, fully automated taxis are more cost-effective than normal taxis.

blocks.text: 題目問： Which of the following statements is accurate?
“To date, Uber has provided a chauffeur-driven taxi service for American clients.”
至今，Uber 為美國客戶提供的是由司機駕駛的的士服務。
“For car users and Uber, it is a win-win situation.”
對汽車使用者和 Uber 來說，這是一個雙贏局面。
只看首尾句，可以先猜 Paragraph 2 會說明 Uber 由傳統有人駕駛服務轉向 driverless taxis 的原因，尤其是雙方可得到的好處。題目問哪一項 accurate，D 提到 cost-effective，最可能在這段找到支援。
題目選項 D 的定位詞是：
“Hiring a driverless cab means that the client does not have to pay for the cost of the driver in the cab fee.”
聘用一輛無人駕駛的士，代表客戶不需要在車費中支付司機成本。
“The only cost incurred by clients is for fuel, plus wear and tear.”
客戶需要承擔的成本只有燃油，加上車輛損耗。
這兩句建立了清楚的成本鏈： driverless cab→ 沒有司機成本→ 客戶只需支付 fuel 和 wear and tear→ 乘車成本有機會比傳統有人駕駛的士低。
題目用 “more cost-effective” 概括原文的成本優勢。原文沒有逐字說 cheaper，但 “does not have to pay for the cost of the driver” 已經直接支援「更具成本效益」。
其他選項： A. Driverless cars conform to safety regulations. Paragraph 4 說現行法律仍要求有 full licence driver 坐在方向盤後，代表 A 和原文不合。
B. There is an obvious market for fully automated cars.原文只說 Uber believes car owners will embrace the idea，這是 Uber 的看法，不足以證明市場obvious。Paragraph 5 還說 Uber 似乎沒有完全信心。
C. Human drivers are no competition for driverless cars.原文說 robot drivers generally safer，但法律仍要求人類司機，沒有說人類司機完全沒有競爭力。

questions.translation: Uber 正投資一項怎樣的技術？

blocks.text: 題目問： Uber is investing in a technology that…
這題要看全文對該技術的總體反應，主要目標段落是 Paragraph 2–5。

Paragraph 2 第一、最後一句顯示 Uber 投入 driverless taxis 的商業動機；Paragraph 3 第一、最後一句顯示 car industry 感到 alarm；Paragraph 4 第一、最後一句顯示 safety 和 legal liability； Paragraph 5 最後一句說這項技術是 doomed venture 還是 universally welcomed depends entirely on your viewpoint。
這些段落合起來呈現的是爭議性，而不是單一正面結果。
“Venturing into the realms of driverless cars is therefore a new direction which will require massive investment.”
進入無人駕駛汽車領域，因此是 Uber 的新方向，並且需要大量投資。
“Not everyone, however, will benefit from this technology.”
不過，並非所有人都會從這項技術受益。
“Apart from the commercial aspect, there is also the issue of safety.”
除了商業層面，還有安全問題。
原文多次顯示這項技術會引起不同立場： 1. Uber 和 car users 可能受益。
3. Taxi drivers 可能失去生計。
5. 法律責任可能變成 lawsuits。
題目 A 說 “will prove controversial”，即會引起爭議。這正好概括全文不同持份者的分歧。
其他選項： B. has been tried and tested Paragraph 2 說 “technology has yet to catch up with the idea of a fully autonomous vehicle”，表示技術仍未成熟到完全自動車階段。
C. is unlikely to prove cost-effective Paragraph 2 說客戶不用支付司機成本，Uber 也可把司機從 payroll 移除，成本方向其實偏正面。
D. will be universally welcomed Paragraph 5 直接說是否 universally welcomed depends entirely on your viewpoint，Paragraph 6 的 John Reynolds 明確反對。

questions.answer: A — They have become a reality in many countries.
questions.answerKey: A — They have become a reality in many countries.
questions.translation: 關於 driverless cars，哪一項不正確？

blocks.text: 題目問： What is NOT true about driverless cars?
“Driverless cars may be set to become a reality.”
無人駕駛汽車可能即將成為現實。
“technology has yet to catch up with the idea of a fully autonomous vehicle.”
技術仍未追上 fully autonomous vehicle 這個想法。
只看這兩處，已經可以判斷：文章說它「可能」成為現實，也說技術尚未完全到位。選項 A 說它已在 many countries 成為現實，方向過強。
“may be set to become a reality”
這裡的 may 很重要，表示可能性，不是既成事實。
原文也沒有 “many countries” 這項資料。
“They have become a reality in many countries.”
這句包含兩個要求： 1. driverless cars 已經成為現實； 2. 這件事發生在 many countries。
原文沒有支援這兩點。相反，文章開首用 “may be set to become a reality”，Paragraph 2 又說fully autonomous vehicle 的技術仍未完全追上概念。因此 A 是 NOT true。
其他選項有原文支援： B. They may improve road safety. Paragraph 4 說：
“Whilst robot drivers, on the whole, are generally safer than their human counterparts…”
整體而言，機械司機通常比人類司機更安全。
C. They will reduce the cost of travelling. Paragraph 2 說客戶不需要支付司機成本，只需承擔燃油和損耗。
D. They will endanger jobs. Paragraph 2 說 taxi drivers 會從 Uber payroll 移除；Paragraph 6 的 John Reynolds 也提到livelihoods。

questions.answer: B — It currently doesn’t favour fully automated cars.
questions.answerKey: B — It currently doesn’t favour fully automated cars.
questions.translation: 關於現行法律，可以怎樣說？

blocks.text: 題目問： What can be said about current legislation?
“Apart from the commercial aspect, there is also the issue of safety.”
除了商業層面，還有安全問題。
“As a consortium of researchers put it, ‘If self-driving cars cut the roughly 40,000 annual US traffic fatalities in half, the car makers might get not 20,000 thank-you notes, but 20,000 lawsuits.’”
正如一個研究者聯盟所說，如果自動駕駛汽車把美國每年約 40,000 宗交通死亡減半，汽車製造商可能收到的不是 20,000 封感謝信，實際可能是 20,000 宗訴訟。
只看首尾句，可以看出 Paragraph 4 集中在安全、法律、責任風險。題目問 legislation，目標段落非常明確。
“Currently, no matter how much automation a car has, the law still requires a driver with a full licence behind the wheel before it can travel on public roads.”
目前，不管汽車有多少自動化功能，法律仍要求有一名持有完整駕照的司機坐在方向盤後，汽車才可以在公共道路上行駛。
這句的主語是 “the law”，也就是現行法律。核心動詞是 “still requires”，表示目前仍然要求人類司機在場。這直接限制 fully automated cars，因為真正的 fully automated car 不需要人類司機在方向盤後。
因此，current legislation 目前不支持完全自動車自由上路。選項 B “currently doesn’t favour fully automated cars” 最貼近。
A. It is in favour of driverless cars.原文方向相反，法律仍要求人類司機。
B. It currently doesn’t favour fully automated cars.正確。
C. It is keeping up with technology.原文沒有說法律正在跟上科技；現行規則仍要求人類司機，反映法律仍限制完全自動化。
D. It already accommodates driverless cars.
“already accommodates” 表示已經容許或配合，和 “law still requires a driver” 不合。所以 30 是 B。

questions.answer: C — The introduction of driverless cars will threaten their livelihoods.
questions.answerKey: C — The introduction of driverless cars will threaten their livelihoods.
questions.translation: 汽車製造商一般持有甚麼看法？

blocks.text: 題目問： What is the general view held by car manufacturers?
“Not everyone, however, will benefit from this technology. The car industry is an obvious example.”
不過，並非所有人都會從這項技術受益。汽車業就是明顯例子。
“As a result, the industry is dragging its feet over the manufacture and introduction of fully automated vehicles onto the market for commercial reasons.”
因此，基於商業原因，汽車業在 fully automated vehicles 的製造和推出市場方面拖慢腳步。
只看首尾句，可以知道這段談的是 car industry 對 driverless cars 的防備心態，尤其是商業利益受威脅。
“Not surprisingly, the industry views the concept of self-driving cars with a sense of growing alarm.”
毫不令人意外，汽車業以日益加深的警覺感看待 self-driving cars 這個概念。
“Such technology could well prove the death knell for private car ownership.”
這種技術很可能成為私人汽車擁有模式的喪鐘。
原文說 car industry 感到 “growing alarm”，原因是 driverless taxis / self-driving cars 可能令私人汽車擁有變得不再必要。一旦 private car ownership 下降，汽車製造商的核心商業模式會受到威脅。
選項 C 說 “threaten their livelihoods”。這裡的 livelihoods 可理解為汽車業賴以生存的商業收入和市場需求。它概括了 “death knell for private car ownership” 和 “commercial reasons”。
其他選項： A. Driverless cars are more dangerous than non-automated cars.安全疑慮在 Paragraph 4 出現，但那是 legislative authorities 和研究者責任問題，並非 car manufacturers 的主要商業立場。
B. Fully automated cars are too expensive to manufacture.原文沒有說製造成本太高。
D. Technology is still too underdeveloped to manufacture driverless cars. Paragraph 2 確實說 technology has yet to catch up，但 Paragraph 3 明確指出 car industry 拖慢推出是 “for commercial reasons”。

questions.answer: B — He reserves judgement as to whether fully automated cars will become a
questions.answerKey: B — He reserves judgement as to whether fully automated cars will become a
questions.translation: 關於作者對 driverless cars 的看法，可以怎樣說？

blocks.text: reality.題目問： What can be said about the writer’s opinion of driverless cars?
“Interestingly, Uber is now undertaking an aggressive hiring campaign for taxi drivers to meet the demand for its taxi app.”
有趣的是，Uber 現在正積極招聘的士司機，以應付其的士 app 的需求。
“Whether Uber is pursuing a doomed venture or is about to introduce a technology that will be universally welcomed depends entirely on your viewpoint.”
Uber 正在追求一項注定失敗的事業，還是即將推出一項會受到普遍歡迎的技術，完全取決於你的觀點。
只看首尾句，可以看到作者保持開放態度：一方面指出 Uber 正投資 driverless cars，另一方面也指出 Uber 仍在聘請司機，並把最終判斷留給不同 viewpoint。
原文最明確的作者態度句是：
“Whether Uber is pursuing a doomed venture or is about to introduce a technology that will be universally welcomed depends entirely on your viewpoint.”
這句提供兩個極端可能： 1. doomed venture：注定失敗的計劃； 2. universally welcomed technology：受普遍歡迎的新科技。
作者沒有明確選其中一方，只說 depends entirely on your viewpoint。這表示作者在這篇文章中保留判斷，呈現不同立場。
選項 B “reserves judgement as to whether fully automated cars will become a reality” 最貼近這種語氣。
其他選項： A. He is uninterested in, but sceptical about, the development of such technology.文章明顯深入討論該技術，不能說 uninterested。
C. He believes that such a technology will never become a reality.原文用 may、depends on your viewpoint，沒有下這種定論。
D. He is critical of Uber’s plans to introduce fully automated cars.作者呈現 Uber、car industry、drivers、residents、teacher 等多方觀點，沒有單方面批評 Uber。

questions.prompt: This person is willing to give up control of their vehicle because they appreciate the benefits of fully automated cars.
questions.translation: 這個人願意放棄自己控制車輛，因為欣賞 fully automated cars 的好處。

blocks.text: “Jason Steiner, a schoolteacher in a Pittsburgh secondary school, is inclined to agree with Susie.”
Jason Steiner 是 Pittsburgh 一所中學的老師，他傾向同意 Susie 的看法。
“I would be slightly wary, though, of being completely dependent on a robot-driven car when it had to react to unexpected obstacles in the road.”
不過，如果要完全依賴一輛 robot-driven car 去應對路上的突發障礙，我會有點警惕。
只看首尾句，可以先估計 Jason 是支持但帶保留的人。他傾向同意 driverless cars 的好處，同時仍有安全疑慮。
“Whilst I’m not averse to driving, I would swap the stressful daily commute by car for a driverless journey if I had the chance!”
雖然我不抗拒開車，但如果有機會，我會把壓力大的每日開車通勤，換成一次無人駕駛旅程。
“It just takes the pressure off driving.”
Jason 說自己 “not averse to driving”，即他並不討厭開車。不過在 daily commute 這個情境下，他願意改乘 driverless journey，原因是它 “takes the pressure off driving”。
題目中的 “give up control of their vehicle” 對應 “swap the stressful daily commute by car for a driverless journey”。題目中的 “appreciate the benefits” 對應 “takes the pressure off driving”。
Susie 也非常支持無人駕駛，但 Question 34 更直接對應她 “never want to drive again”。
Question 33 的「因為欣賞 fully automated cars 的好處而願意在某些情境下交出控制權」更貼近Jason。

questions.prompt: This person would have no regrets about giving up driving entirely in favour of being driven by a fully automated car.
questions.translation: 這個人若完全放棄開車、改由 fully automated car 接送，也不會後悔。

blocks.text: “Susie Greenacre, a resident of Pittsburgh, has no such reservations about driverless cars.”
Pittsburgh 居民 Susie Greenacre 對 driverless cars 沒有這些保留。
“I think if I could just hop in a driverless car which would take me anywhere I wanted, I would never want to drive again!”
我想，如果我可以直接坐進一輛無人駕駛車，讓它帶我去任何我想去的地方，我便再也不想開車了。
“I would never want to drive again!”
“never want to drive again” 比 “give up driving entirely” 更強。Susie 的語氣非常明確：她不只願意試用 driverless car，更說如果可以讓車帶她去任何地方，她便不想再駕駛。她的前一句也支援這種態度：“I’m all for it. Driverless cars have my backing, any day!”
我完全支持。Driverless cars 任何時候都得到我的支持。
題目說 “would have no regrets about giving up driving entirely”，這是對 Susie 態度的合理概括。

questions.prompt: This person is aware that the new technology of driverless cars may not provide an adequate substitute for a human driver.
questions.translation: 這個人意識到 driverless cars 這項新技術，可能未必能完全取代人類司機。

blocks.text: “Jason Steiner, a schoolteacher in a Pittsburgh secondary school, is inclined to agree with Susie.”
Jason Steiner 是 Pittsburgh 一所中學的老師，他傾向同意 Susie 的看法。
“I would be slightly wary, though, of being completely dependent on a robot-driven car when it had to react to unexpected obstacles in the road.”
不過，如果要完全依賴 robot-driven car 來應對道路上的突發障礙，我會有點警惕。
原文沒有直接說 human driver substitute，但有：
Jason 的疑慮很清楚：在一般情況下，他願意乘坐 driverless journey；可是遇到 unexpected obstacles，他對完全依賴 robot-driven car 有保留。
題目把這句概括成：無人駕駛技術可能未必完全足以取代人類司機。這是短距離推論，因為如果robot-driven car 面對突發障礙的反應令人擔心，就代表它仍可能不如人類司機靈活。

questions.prompt: This person believes that those affected adversely by new technology should be protected from its effects.
questions.translation: 這個人認為，受到新科技不利影響的人應得到保護。

blocks.text: “John Reynolds, a Pittsburgh taxi driver, is angry at Uber’s attitude towards fully automated technology.”
Pittsburgh 的士司機 John Reynolds 對 Uber 對 fully automated technology 的態度感到憤怒。
“I guess I’m biased, being a taxi driver myself, but it’s difficult to see it objectively.”
我想我自己是的士司機，所以有偏見，但要客觀看待這件事很難。
只看首尾句，可以看出 John 是受直接影響的一方。他的觀點圍繞 livelihoods 和保障。
“there should be some safeguards in place to protect those potentially affected by the introduction of new technologies.”
應該設有一些保障措施，以保護那些可能受到新科技引入影響的人。
題目中的 “protected from its effects” 對應原文 “safeguards in place to protect”。
題目中的 “those affected adversely” 對應原文 “those potentially affected”。
“They are completely disregarding individual livelihoods, such as mine…”
他們完全忽視個人生計，例如我的生計。
這說明他擔心新科技損害司機和汽車業相關人士的生活。因此 Question 36 明確對應 John Reynolds。

questions.prompt: This person enjoys driving but only under favourable conditions.
questions.translation: 這個人喜歡或至少不抗拒開車，但只在較理想情況下如此。

blocks.text: “Jason Steiner, a schoolteacher in a Pittsburgh secondary school, is inclined to agree with Susie.”
Jason Steiner 是 Pittsburgh 一所中學的老師，他傾向同意 Susie。
“I would be slightly wary, though, of being completely dependent on a robot-driven car when it had to react to unexpected obstacles in the road.”
不過，如果要完全依賴 robot-driven car 去應對道路上的突發障礙，我會有點警惕。
“Whilst I’m not averse to driving, I would swap the stressful daily commute by car for a driverless journey if I had the chance!”
雖然我不抗拒開車，但如果有機會，我會把壓力大的每日開車通勤，換成一次無人駕駛旅程。

“not averse to driving” 表示他不討厭駕駛，甚至可以接受駕駛。題目用 “enjoys driving” 稍微概括得較正面，但在三位人物中，只有 Jason 同時表示自己不排斥開車，又明確不想承受 stressful daily commute。“only under favourable conditions” 對應的是：他願意駕駛，但不想面對壓力大的通勤。當駕駛變成 stressful daily commute，他寧願選 driverless journey。 Susie 是完全想放棄駕駛；John 則主要談工作和保障。因此 37 最貼近 Jason。所以 37 是 C。

questions.prompt: Driverless technology will have to overcome legal and safety obstacles to become completely viable.
questions.translation: Driverless technology 若要完全可行，必須克服法律和安全障礙。

blocks.text: “Apart from the commercial aspect, there is also the issue of safety.”
除了商業層面，還有安全問題。
“As a consortium of researchers put it, ‘If self-driving cars cut the roughly 40,000 annual US traffic fatalities in half, the car makers might get not 20,000 thank-you notes, but 20,000 lawsuits.’”
正如一個研究者聯盟所說，如果自動駕駛汽車把美國每年約 40,000 宗交通死亡減半，汽車製造商可能收到的不是 20,000 封感謝信，實際可能是 20,000 宗訴訟。
“Whilst a fully automated car could respond to most eventualities in the course of a trip, would it be capable of responding to unforeseen events, such as changes in route or unexpected diversions?”
雖然 fully automated car 可能能應付旅途中大部分情況，但它是否有能力應對不可預見事件，例如路線改變或突發改道？
“Currently, no matter how much automation a car has, the law still requires a driver with a full licence behind the wheel before it can travel on public roads.”
目前，不管汽車自動化程度有多高，法律仍要求有一名持有完整駕照的司機坐在方向盤後，汽車才可在公共道路上行駛。
題目有兩個核心部分： 1. safety obstacles 2. legal obstacles原文第一句 “the issue of safety” 直接支援 safety obstacles；後面提到 unforeseen events、route changes、unexpected diversions，說明技術仍面對安全情境挑戰。
法律方面，原文說現行法律仍要求持牌司機在方向盤後，這正好是 fully automated cars 上路的legal obstacle。
題目說 “will have to overcome… to become completely viable”，雖然原文沒有逐字說 completely viable，但整段的意思就是：若安全和法律問題未解決，fully automated cars 難以正式上路和普遍使用。

questions.prompt: Uber has shown complete confidence in its investment in driverless cars.
questions.translation: Uber 對自己投資 driverless cars 顯示出完全信心。

blocks.text: “Interestingly, Uber is now undertaking an aggressive hiring campaign for taxi drivers to meet the demand for its taxi app.”
有趣的是，Uber 現在正積極招聘的士司機，以應付其的士 app 的需求。
“Whether Uber is pursuing a doomed venture or is about to introduce a technology that will be universally welcomed depends entirely on your viewpoint.”
Uber 正在追求一項注定失敗的事業，還是即將推出一項會受普遍歡迎的技術，完全取決於你的觀點。
“It seems that even Uber is less than confident that driverless taxis will soon become a reality.”
看來連 Uber 也沒有十足信心認為 driverless taxis 很快會成為現實。
題目說 “complete confidence”，是非常強的程度詞。原文說 “less than confident”，意思是信心不足或沒有完全信心。這是明確相反方向。
題目命題： Uber has shown complete confidence.原文命題： Even Uber is less than confident.兩者直接衝突。
前一句 “aggressive hiring campaign for taxi drivers” 也支援這點：如果 Uber 正積極聘請人類司機，代表它仍需要傳統有人駕駛服務來滿足需求，無人駕駛的士未能即時取代現有模式。

questions.prompt: The safety issues with driverless technology are likely to be resolved fairly quickly.
questions.translation: Driverless technology 的安全問題很可能會相當快地解決。

blocks.text: “Apart from the commercial aspect, there is also the issue of safety.”
除了商業層面，還有安全問題。
“As a consortium of researchers put it, ‘If self-driving cars cut the roughly 40,000 annual US traffic fatalities in half, the car makers might get not 20,000 thank-you notes, but 20,000 lawsuits.’”
正如一個研究者聯盟所說，即使 self-driving cars 可把美國每年約 40,000 宗交通死亡減半，汽車製造商可能面對的仍可能是訴訟。
“there is also the issue of safety”
“would it be capable of responding to unforeseen events…”
它是否能應對不可預見事件……
原文確實說明安全問題存在，也說 legislative authorities share these safety concerns。不過題目問的是解決速度：
“are likely to be resolved fairly quickly”
這需要原文提供時間預測，例如 soon、quickly、in the near future、within a short time 等。文章沒有提供這類資料。
原文也沒有說安全問題會長期無法解決。它只指出存在安全疑慮和法律責任問題。因此不能選FALSE；因為 FALSE 需要原文明確提供相反方向，例如安全問題不可能很快解決。文章沒有這樣定論。
資料清單：原文有：● 安全問題存在；● 無人車能否處理 unforeseen events 仍有疑問；● legislative authorities share safety concerns；● 法律責任可能導致 lawsuits。
原文缺少：● safety issues 會否解決；● 解決需時多久；● 是否 fairly quickly。
Final Answers 27. D 28. A 29. A 30. B 31. C 32. B 33. C 34. B 35. C 36. A 37. C 38. TRUE 39. FALSE 40. NOT GIVEN

paragraphOverview.title: Skim Roadmap：只看每段首尾句後可合理看
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: 首句說 driverless cars 可能即將成為現實，至少 Uber 高層似乎這樣相信；尾句說 Uber Advanced Technologies Centre 的終極目標是研究 mapping、vehicle safety 和 autonomy technology。只看首尾句，可以估計本段功能是介紹 Uber 正投入無人駕駛技術研發，並把文章焦點放在「driverless cars 是否會成真」。這段偏向背景引入，適合定位 Uber、research centre、autonomy technology 等資料。

首句說 Uber 至今提供的是 chauffeur-driven taxi service；尾句說對 car users 和 Uber 來說， driverless taxis 是 win-win situation。只看首尾句，可以估計本段會講 Uber 從有人駕駛的士轉向無人駕駛的士的商業邏輯。中間應該會出現投資風險、技術現況、成本節省、車主或乘客利益，以及 Uber 可從 payroll 移除司機等內容。
首句用轉折指出，並非所有人都會從這項技術受益，car industry 是明顯例子；尾句說汽車業基於商業理由拖慢 fully automated vehicles 的製造和推出。只看首尾句，可見本段處理反對或受威脅的一方：汽車製造業擔心自動駕駛會削弱私人汽車擁有模式，因此對技術抱有 growing alarm。
首句說除了商業層面，還有 safety issue；尾句引用研究者指出，即使 self-driving cars 可把美國每年約 40,000 宗交通死亡減半，汽車製造商可能收到的不是感謝信，而是訴訟。只看首尾句，可以估計本段集中在安全和法律障礙：自動車能否處理突發事件、現行法律是否容許、責任如何分配，都是關鍵問題。
首句說有趣的是，Uber 現在正積極聘請 taxi drivers 以應付 app 需求；尾句說 Uber 的計劃到底是 doomed venture，還是 universally welcomed technology，完全取決於觀點。只看首尾句，可見本段在平衡全文語氣：連 Uber 自己也似乎未完全確定無人駕駛的士能否很快成真，作者沒有直接替讀者定案。
首句說 Pittsburgh taxi driver John Reynolds 對 Uber 對 fully automated technology 的態度感到憤怒；尾句說他承認自己是 taxi driver，可能有偏見，也難以客觀看待。只看首尾句，可以估計本段是受威脅工作者的觀點：他擔心個人生計、大型汽車製造商利益，以及新科技推出時缺少對受影響者的保障。

首句說 Pittsburgh 居民 Susie Greenacre 對 driverless cars 沒有這些保留；尾句說若她能直接坐進一輛 driverless car 去任何地方，她便再也不想開車。只看首尾句，可見本段是支持者觀點：她討厭 rush-hour traffic，覺得 driverless cars 能減少駕駛壓力。她的態度非常正面，適合定位 no regrets / never drive again 類題目。
首句說 Pittsburgh secondary school teacher Jason Steiner 傾向同意 Susie；尾句說他會稍微擔心完全依賴 robot-driven car，尤其當它需要應對路上 unexpected obstacles。只看首尾句，可見本段是較溫和的支持者：他不抗拒開車，但願意用無人駕駛取代壓力大的通勤；同時保留安全疑慮，特別是突發障礙處理能力。
